sources.title: The Analects
sources.author: Confucius
sources.excerpt: Is it not a pleasure, having learned something, to try it out at due intervals? Is it not a joy to have friends come from afar? Is one human who does not know yet does not resent it, not a gentleman?
sources.longExcerpt: Is it not a pleasure, having learned something, to try it out at due intervals? Is it not a joy to have friends come from afar? Is one human who does not know yet does not resent it, not a gentleman? These opening lines of the Analects encapsulate Confucian ideals about learning, friendship, and proper conduct. This foundational text of Chinese philosophy from around 500 BCE shaped East Asian thought for millennia, emphasizing moral cultivation, social harmony, and the importance of education.

sources.title: Records of the Grand Historian
sources.author: Sima Qian
sources.excerpt: When the Grand Historian wrote this work, he was cut off from his generation. He dwelt in sorrow and anger, yet his will became all the stronger. He wished to set forth the true facts for later generations.
sources.longExcerpt: When the Grand Historian wrote this work, he was cut off from his generation. He dwelt in sorrow and anger, yet his will became all the stronger. He wished to set forth the true facts for later generations. This monumental historical work from 94 BCE covers over 2,000 years of Chinese history, from the Yellow Emperor to Emperor Wu of Han, establishing the template for all subsequent Chinese historical writing.
